must_file: Your card has expired or will expire within the next six months
Your card was lost, stolen, mutilated or destroyed
You got the card before you turned 14 and have now turned 14, unless the card expires before your 16th birthday
You have legally changed your name or other biographic information
Your card has wrong information on it
You never received the card USCIS issued
You were a commuter and now live in the United States, or the other way round
Your status was automatically converted to permanent resident status
You still hold an old card (Form AR-3, AR-103 or I-151), which is no longer valid
receipt_text: This notice, together with your Form I-551, Permanent Resident Card (also known as the Green Card), provides evidence of your lawful permanent resident status for 36 months from the expiration date on your Permanent Resident Card. You remain authorized to work and travel.

reading.title: Green Card Renewal: Cost, Timeline, and How To Apply
reading.checked: Its fees ($415 online, $465 on paper), the six-month filing window, the 36-month receipt extension and the rule that two-year cards go to Form I-751 all match USCIS as read on this page's date. Its processing-time estimates are the firm's own and are not used here.

reading.title: How to Remove the Conditions on My Green Card
reading.checked: The 90-day filing window before a two-year card expires matches the USCIS conditional residence page. Its I-751 fees and wait times are the firm's own figures and are not used here.
